why:
RFC-0033 `view` mode (issue 0007 / phase 229.6) -- a subscription whose callback receives `&B::View<'a>`, a message whose unbounded sequence and string fields point directly into the receive buffer with no `heapless::Vec` copy, valid for the callback's duration only. rclrs has nothing of the kind: its one zero-copy affordance is `PublisherState::borrow_loaned_message` on the PUBLISH side, and its subscriptions always deserialise into an owned message. The constraint is the same one the rest of this lane records -- no allocator, so the alternative to viewing in place is a fixed-capacity copy that has to be sized for the worst case at build time. QoS is forced to KEEP_LAST(1) (the triple buffer gives the callback one well-defined slot); a view subscription registered with a deeper queue is REJECTED rather than silently downgraded.

On `nros::Node`, the executor-borrowing node handle (`exec.node_mut(id)`); it was `NodeCtx` until phase-483 W2, which the correlator folded onto `Node` (`TYPE_SYNONYMS`). MEASURABLE ONLY SINCE 2026-09-12: `nros_node::executor`'s `mod node` kept the type private while `Executor::node_mut` returned it, so every method on it was callable and none of them had ever produced a row -- issue 1351.
